prompts.name: castle-cliffs-left
prompts.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. EDIT the supplied isolated castle/cliffs layer into a directional lightning lighting state. Output 1536x1024 transparent PNG with exactly the same full-canvas registration, silhouette, castle scale, perspective, masonry, trees, zigzag path, bottom cutoff, and rock positions. Change ONLY the illumination.
A powerful lightning flash is OFF SCREEN TO THE LEFT, slightly above the horizon. Left-facing walls of the castle towers, left-facing rock facets, and left-facing edges of the stone path flare pale white with fine black stipple/engraving still visible. Right-facing walls and rock fissures remain deep opaque BLACK, including the right sides of the round towers. Sharp directional contrast following each object's shape, NOT a global image inversion or a simple left-to-right overlay. All forms must remain identical; no added towers, windows, boulders, branches, lightning bolts or scenery.
Keep the original tiny monochrome stipple and hatch detail at the same scale. The actual subject remains positioned in the right half and lower-right part of the canvas, unchanged. Outside the original castle/cliff/tree silhouette is genuine transparent alpha; if the reference preview appears gray outside the subject, that gray is only the transparency preview and must NOT be painted into the output. Interior black shadows stay opaque. No glow halo, sky, moon, mountains, lake, foreground, captions, text or checkerboard. The output will be swapped over the base image, so precise registration is essential.

prompts.name: mountains-trees-left
prompts.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. EDIT the most recent supplied background-mountains-and-trees image into a screen-left lightning illumination state. Output transparent 1536x1024 PNG with EXACTLY the same full-canvas registration, ridge silhouettes, individual peaks, pine-tree silhouettes, horizon position, forests, and composition. The gray area above the ridges in this preview represents transparency: it must be fully transparent alpha in the output, never a painted sky.
Change ONLY the lighting. A strong off-screen lightning flash from far LEFT grazes the LEFT-facing facets of every mountain: those slopes flare much brighter, white with fine dark stipple and hatch detail. RIGHT-facing mountain facets stay deep black. Left-facing edges of the pine crowns and trunks gain fine white rim highlights while their right halves stay black. Keep the white valley mist as in the original without making the whole image white. Strength should read instantly as a flash from LEFT, not uniform brightening or a negative/inversion. The rightmost trees and slopes should stay comparatively dark, with lit left edges only.
Preserve all original silhouettes and exact object positions. Keep the original tiny black-and-white Macintosh pen-and-ink dot scale and sharp engraving. Below the existing straight horizon, retain the opaque black fill to the bottom. No new objects, sky, glow halo, bolts, moon, stars, lake, castle, foreground, text or checkerboard. True transparent alpha above the original silhouette; black shadows INSIDE the silhouette remain opaque. This image swaps directly over the original layer, so registration must not shift.

prompts.name: lake-left
prompts.prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. EDIT the supplied WATER-ONLY image to show a brief lightning illumination from OFF SCREEN LEFT. Output 1536x1024 landscape PNG. Keep exactly the same shallow-angle water perspective, fine horizontal ripple scale and phase, overall ripple positions, and the narrow vertical moon reflection around 70% width. No shoreline or other objects.
The lightning adds a distinct broad, broken SILVER-WHITE REFLECTION on the LEFT third of the lake. The left-facing facets of wavelets catch the light: very bright but finely engraved horizontal dashes, densely concentrated toward upper-left and fanning subtly toward lower-left. Brightness falls off through center; the RIGHT third remains nearly BLACK aside from the existing slender moon reflection. Dark troughs remain black between bright wave crests, even in the illuminated left region. This must be a physically directional relighting with highlighted wave facets, NOT an inverted/negative image, not a uniform brightness wash or smooth gradient overlay.
Preserve the existing water geometry and subtle 1980s Macintosh fine monochrome stipple and linework. No new waves of a different scale, no vertical lightning-bolt reflection, no visible bolt, no sky, land, moon disc, mountains, cliffs, foreground, text or border. Opaque black water fills every pixel to all four edges. Render the same lake surface with changed illumination only.

prompts.name: foreground-left
prompts.prompt: Use case: lighting-weather. Asset: foreground lightning state for a layered monochrome engraved castle scene. EDIT the provided foreground image, preserving EXACT full-canvas 1536x1024 registration, identical tree trunk and branch silhouette, identical rocks, reeds, grasses, shoreline edge, crop and perspective. Change ONLY illumination. A sharp lightning flash comes from OFF SCREEN LEFT. Add narrow bright engraved highlights on LEFT-facing bark ridges, branches, rock facets and reeds. Most foreground remains opaque BLACK. Crucially DARKEN the RIGHT-facing surfaces substantially compared with the current image: remove the existing bright right-side moonlight edges, right-facing rock facets and the bright grass on the lower-right shoreline. The right shoreline should be predominantly black, with only sparse narrow highlights on its left-facing edges. Maintain fine stipple detail at exactly the source scale. Do not simply brighten the entire tree or invert colors. No broad glow or haze. Actual transparent alpha everywhere outside the original foreground silhouette, including between branches and the large empty central opening; gray in a preview represents transparency, not a sky. All interior shadow blacks stay opaque. No new branches, objects, moon, stars, clouds, mountains, castle, water, text, bolts or backdrop. Keep the exact same composition so this can replace the base foreground during a synchronized flash.
